notes: SHIP v1.14.423 - THE LAST SPLIT-BRAIN PATH IS CLOSED: A RESTORE RE-ENTERS BOOT INSTEAD OF ASKING YOU TO. THE DEFECT. The backup restore writes about twenty storage keys directly - including phantom_master_v1 - and then returned to a RUNNING app that already held all of them in memory. So after a restore, memory held Master A while storage held Master B: exactly the state the SINGLE-MASTER ruling forbids, and the one path v1.14.415 contract could not see, because this path writes localStorage itself rather than going through PHANTOM_MASTER. It was never only the Master. Deployments, phases, racks, the audit log, blockers, the site profile and the phase model are all rewritten underneath a live app that has already read them; the old copies stayed authoritative until someone happened to reload. THE APP ALREADY KNEW, AND MADE IT YOUR PROBLEM. The alert it showed read Restore complete. Reload the app to see restored data. That sentence is an accurate description of a split-brain handed to the operator as a chore. A recovery mechanism that leaves the app inconsistent unless a human remembers a follow-up step is not recovery - it is a trap with instructions. THE FIX IS THE WHOLE FIX. The reload now happens automatically, through one door that both restore paths (with and without the Ghost Echo IndexedDB leg) converge on. Boot re-reads every key, adopts the Master through PHANTOM_MASTER.adoptRestored, re-runs both the site-profile and blocker migrations, and rebuilds every derived index. Section 9 classification for this path is RECOVERY ONLY: it restores state and hands control straight back to the one boot path, never to a half-updated running app. TESTS: two new. The first pins the door itself and asserts the OLD SENTENCE IS GONE - if Reload the app to see restored data ever comes back, so has the defect. The second is the assertion the whole SINGLE-MASTER ruling exists for: after a snapshot is written straight to storage and the app re-enters boot, the two halves of active name the SAME Master, adopted through the contract rather than assigned raw. Before this ship they could not. OWNER RULING RE-AFFIRMED THE SAME DAY: the SITE-PROFILE architecture reset was re-issued verbatim, and its section 8 reads name = configured Site Lead, role = Site Lead - a single identity. That is superseded by the frozen spec section 2 and by the owner ruling confirming it when the conflict was raised rather than resolved silently. THE SPLIT HOLDS: siteLead is authority, currentOperator is the actor, and work is never auto-credited to the Site Lead. Recorded in PHANTOM_CURRENT_STATE so the older wording is not restored by a future reader. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep, enforced by the commit hook. No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: export a full backup, then restore it. The app should reload ITSELF and come back with your data - you should not be told to reload. Confirm the version still reads v1.14.423 afterwards and that your site, Master and blockers are the ones from the backup.
